cells.date: Śaka 888, Kārttika, Vaiśākha, Paurṇamī, Wednesday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Vaṇikāpuṇḍi situated in the Rēpaka-12 in Sabbi-1000 by Ārikēsarin of the Chālukya family of Lēmūlāvaṁśa whose genealogy is given and who is described as a feudatory of the Râshṭrakūṭa king. The gift was made for the purpose of worship in and repairs to the Subhadhāma-jinālaya constructed at the donor's father Baddoga at Lēmūlāpāṭaka. The donee was Sōmadēvasūri, the author of Yaśōdhara-charita. The record was composed by poet Peddaṇa and engraved by Rēva. Published in the Chālukyas of Vēṁulavāḍa, pp. 92 ff.

cells.place: Plates in the possession of Tonappa Parisa Upadhye. Through Dr. B. R. Gopal.
cells.date: Śaka 910, Sarvadhāri, Kārttika śu. 5, Monday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: States that three individuals, Nāgai-śrēshṭhi, Lōkkai-śrēshṭhi and Ādityavarman paid 40 dīnāras to the king for confirming their rights on the villages Kīṇijala and Puḷisa which had come to their family by heredity. Also records a gift of one lakh of betel-nuts on this same occasion to a certain Dēvapāla, son of Vāmaṇa, composed the record which was engraved by Vaijada. The earlier part of the record contains the genealogical account of the Râshṭrakūṭa and Śilāhāra dynasties.

cells.remarks: Records the capture of the hill fortress of Pāṅgallu from the Muḥammadans on the specified date by Immadi Bukka, the brother (anuja) of Irugapa-daṇḍanāthēśvara and son of Baicha-daṇḍādhipa and the renovation of the fort, the embellishment of the city with a padmākāra (tank), a vēpī (well) etc., by him. cells.place:
Gāngāpuram.—Three sides of a slab by
the side of Benakāya-guți in front of
the Chennakēśava temple.
cells.date:
[Śrī]mukha, Phāl-
guna śu... Thurs-
day. Uttarāyana-
sańkrānti.
cells.remarks: Top portion broken and damaged. Refers to the construction of a Jina-griha and the consecration of the image of Channa- Pārśvanātha theren by mahādandanāyaka Manigāra Kāmaņa to whom the king granted an income from levies and commodities such as areca etc., for the inversion of an offering to the same. Mentions the officers aṁkādhikārī and addasunkad-adhikāri. Contains an eulogy of Nayakīrtidēva who perhaps the recipient of the gift and refers to the Chālukya dynasty of whom Tailapa is mentioned. Garigā- Puram is also described. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.place: Slab set up near the tank called Nain-bulakuṇṭa. First face.
cells.date: Year 6, Rudhirōdgāri, Srāvaṇa-puṇṇame, Wednesday, lunar eclipse = 1143 A.D., July 28.
cells.remarks: The first portion of the record states that Vāvanaya, the brother-in-law of mahāpradhāna manevergade daṇḍanāyaka sahasāsi Bhimanayya, made a gift of lands to god Bhīmēsvara and also land to the tank called Nainbula-kuṇṭa. The latter part states that Mallahampādēvi, daughter of Vaṇ-karaschōla-mahārāja and Padmaladēvi constructed the temple. The latter was the daughter of mahamaṇḍalēśvara Nīlakaṇṭhadēvarasa of the Ayyana-vamśa, and Mahādēvi. In characters of about the 11th century. Published in A. P. Govt. Archl.Series, op. cit., Mn. 50, pp. 36-37.

cells.location: Kolanupāka-contd.
cells.place: Pillars in the compound of the Sōmēś-vara temple. Third pillar. (Museum No. 83)
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a canal named Vāniśavardhani in Kolīpāka by Pōti-nāyaka, son of Machi-nāyaka and Mādachi, and the servant of Induśēkhara of the Chālukya family and also a gift of 30 nivartanas of land by him (Pōti-nāyaka) to god Sōmēśvara. Gives details of various servants serving in the temple and also, for worship and offerings to the god. Gives an account of this branch of the Chālukyas and their relationship with the queen Rudrāmbā (cf. No. A. 19). Published in HAS, No. 13, pp. 82 ff.

cells.place: Fourth pillar. (Museum No. 84)
cells.remarks: Records the gift of land including the one-third portion of the royal dues from the tadayari formerly granted to the Chēnimōche (?) basadi in agrahāra Tandipāmu-laṅka which was a prabhūta-agrahāra of Sōmanātha-bhaṭṭa and was included in Kāviradēśa-40, to god Sōmēśvara. States that from the king and at the instance of mahāpradhāna antahpurap-vergade Kālimayya and his younger brother Tikkapayya who was the dandāṇyaka of Kolīpāka-7000. Prince Sōmēśvara is stated to have been ruling over several territories including Kolīpāka-nāḍu.

cells.remarks: Registers gifts of land at three mattar apiece as sandhivigrahi daṇḍanāyaka Kūlimayya to (i) god Mallikārjunadēva installed by his younger brother Tikkapayya, the daṇḍanāyaka of Kollipāka-nagara and (ii) Mallikārjunadēva at the same place installed by his son-in-law prathamika Rummaddēva-sōmayāji, and (iii) Svayampāki Mallu-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya, with the permission of the king. Besides 40 nivartanas of wet land and two house-sites were granted to each of the above mentioned donees in their respective villages.

cells.place: Slab built into the wall of the main shrine of the Viranārāyaṇasvāmin temple. Proper left.
cells.date: Chālukya - Vikrama year 29, Tāraṇa, Chaitra, Pūrṇimā, Sunday, lunar eclipse=1104 A. D., March 13.
cells.remarks: Gives a lengthy description of the Arbuda mountain and an account of the Paramāra rulers down to Jagadēva who, on the orders of the king granted the village Piriya-Pembariti, one of the twelve villages included in Kollipāka-dēśa excluding from it the lands that were already given to god Ānandēśvara and the gardens for the worship of the god and upkeep of the temple and the feeding of ascetics at Jagadēva-nārāyāpura built by Sōmala-daṇḍanāyaka. Records in addition, the grant of Uttamaganda-chinhas at the rate of five, four and three from all the villages of Kollipāka-7000, named after each one of the three principal chiefs and adhīkāra respectively and some lands in Nidungūru and [Rāmala?]cheruvu to the west of Jagadēvava-tāṭaka for certain other services such as supply of garlands, fruits, etc. Published in Andhra Pradesh Govt. Archl. Series, No. 3 (Kannada Inscriptions of Andhra Pradesh), Ng. 45, pp. 57-61.

cells.place: Four faces of a pillar in the tank behind the Sōmēśvara temple.
cells.date: Chālukya - Vikrama 50, Viśvāvasu, Chaitra ba. 3, Monday = f.d.t. 6, March 23, f.d.t. '06.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Pāṇpura, excluding the dēvabhōga land formerly granted to Ākka-basadi near Poḷaln, to the goddess Ambikādēvī of Ambaraśilāka by prince Sōmarasa who was ruling from Kalyāṇapura under mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Siriyayya. Kēśirāja who was the pergade of the goddess (dēviya-pergaḍe), was to be in charge of the gift. On three of its faces the pillar contains the praśastis of Kammāra, Sōmēśvara, Svāmi-daṇḍādhipa and the Jaina pontiffs belonging to Dēvagaṇa and Sarasvati-gaṇa of Balatkara-gaṇa. Also mentions the construction of a māṇastambha and a makara-toraṇa to the temple of the goddess by Kēśirāja.

cells.place: Pillar near a stream called Peddavagu
cells.date: Śaka 989, Plava-raṅga, Kārttika śu. 13, Monday = 1067 A.D., October 22, f. d. t. '20.
cells.remarks: Records the restoration of some lands in Juvvikunte and Nidungūru originally granted by Saṅkaraṅgaṇa of the Rāshṭrakūṭa family by a copper-plate charter to the basadis at Rēvuṇḍi and Nērilā built by him and subsequently alienated from the basadis unjustly, by the queen at the request of rahasyādhikārin Anantapāla-daṇḍanāyaka and on the representation of Robbiseya and the korrasa added by pergade Appanayya on the occasion of a solar eclipse. Mahāmāmanta Mējarasa was then governing Koḷipāka-7000.

cells.place: Pillar in front of the Hanumāna temple
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Sandarahāṁļu (?) in Koulade-12 as tadvartin to Rāmésvara-pandita, disciple of Téjonidhi- paņdita of the Kūlaimukha sect for worship and offerings, feeding the students and maintaining a satra in the temple of Utteśvara by Muddaya, the mahāpradhāna of Kandūru who was governing Kollipāke-7000. Mentions Rudra-padya-pandita as the predecessor of Téjonidhi-pandita. Further, gifts of money from the officials are also recorded.

cells.remarks: Fragmentary. cells.remarks: Records that perggaḍe Jōgappayya having renovated the temple of Indranārāyaṇa formerly built by king Indravallabha of the Rashtrakūta family in rājadhāni Bōdhana, consecrated the image of Vishnu therein, erected a Garuda-pillar and granted lands to gods Priyā-Māvudge and Kiriyā-Māvudge in Pōsay-70 village, with houses, sites, a flower-garden and income from the toll on salt for the worship of the god. cells.date:

sākha ba. 13, Wed-
nesday=923 A.D.,
April 20.
cells.remarks: Broken into two pieces and incomplete. Mentions bhūpati Sāvaṭa. Records the installation of the image and the construction of the temple by the minister (mantrin) Sātyapura, belonging to a famous Jaina architect, belonging to the Dharkaṭa- family hailing from Parnaṭalaka, son of Dēdūlaka and grandson of Ārabhata, at the instance of Pulindra who is described as ruler (mahī-bhṛt). Also mentions Varāṅga, son of Śarvadēva, and Sūrasēna, the Jaina teacher. The praśasti was composed by Sigarapaṇḍi and Lōkadēva.

cells.location: Chidambaram
cells.place: Naṭarāja temple, second prākāra, east wall.
cells.date: Year 6, Mīna śu. Paurnamī, Wednesdaụ, Hastam = 1255 A.D., March 24.
cells.remarks: Records that the 500 neḷ of tax-free land, originally endowed by Araiyan Periyanāyan alias Gaṅgaiyarāyan of Enādi-Meṛkuḍi in Tirukkalakuḷamā nādu for supply of offerings in the temple during three specified dates subsequent to resulting in the reduction in the supply of fruits, was now made once again tax-free on which the mahāsabhā of Śrī Vīranārāyaṇam alias Sundarapāṇḍya-chaturvēdimangalam agreed to supply to the temple of Tiruchchigrambalam-uḍaiyār a specific sum of fruits for the daily use as well as for the various festivals in the temple.

cells.place: Maṇḍapa called Nṛitta-sabhā Kāilāsa, in the same prākāra. Slab paved into the floor.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land, purchased from one of the Tillai-mūnāyiravar of the temple, to provide for offerings to Naṭarāja on Tiruvādirai festivals and passage of ammadhi-bhiksham by a certain Iṭṭilikkombi Achchan. After the offering the food was to be distributed to the Tillai-mūnāyiravar. The donor claims to be the son of Niḷichchi and to have caused a temple to be built at Kaḷpātti. In late characters.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of 10 mā of land, bought from several individuals to provide for offerings to the image of the deity carved in the maṇḍapa, by Araiyan Uyyavandān-Kiruṇa[n]ṇāmbi alias Nōkkalāgiyān-mahā at Perumparappuliyūr for the well-being of Perumāl by Uyyavandān Tirunōkkalaigiyān Ṭoṇḍaimān of Mañjakkuddi. Refers to the land granted to Kanakabhāshapati-paṇḍitar who composed a kāvya on the mālā-parishad of the place.

In characters of about the 13th century.

cells.place: Third prākāra. Maṇḍapa to the north of the Subrahmanya shrine near the western gōpura, tiers.
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. Records the order of Pallavadaraiyar probably in respect of the details of organisation of a Sarasvatī-bhaṇḍāram and a grant for maintaining and expanding the same. The Sarasvatī-bhaṇḍāram seems to have been established by Svāmīdēvar. Enumerates the names of twenty scholars employed in the above bhaṇḍāram and also to have been the place for keeping the temple granthas. The title anaittulagam-koṇḍaruliya of the king occurs in the body of the text. In characters of about the 13th century.

Central shrine, east wall, base
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records several gifts of land by Kulikkōyiḽ, the wife of..... cells.location: Māḍambākkam
cells.place: Same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of the levies such as kāṇikkai, mariyādai and āśuvāi from the village to god Sirrēri-āḷuḍaiya-nāyaṉār for the purpose of burning a perpetual lamp and light-lamps during the Amāvāsyai-ayanam-pūjais. Further records that the kaṭṭalai-kārar, maḍhapatis (barber) and veṭṭiyān should be taken into the temple treasury and used for repairs in the temple. Mentions a Vimārāśa (Bhīmarāja).

cells.location: Māḍambākkam
cells.place: South wall (outside) of the same prākāra
cells.remarks: Do. Refers to some arrangement made by an assembly of the Rudra-Śrī-Māhēśvaras in connection with the lands probably in Utipākkam-agaram-uḍaiyār or in Tiruppuḷiyūr-kkōṭṭam-uḍaiyār-nāḍu. Punṉeri alias Araśanārāyaṇa-choṭaturvēdi-maṅgalam, belonging to the deities Kayilāsamuḍaiya-nāyaṉār, Tiruvagattīśvaramuḍaiya-nāyaṉār and Poy[y*]jillēva-ramuḍaiya-nāyaṉār. Also seems to refer to an agreement by Ayyava-Piḷḷai, Māhēśvaras, Tīrthattār and Niyāyattār. Mentions also Poṭṭappi-māriyār of the village. Do.

In characters of about the 15th century.

In characters of about the 13th century.

In characters of about the 11th century.

cells.remarks: Consists of many fragments. One piece mentions the ūrār of Kirankudi and another the ūrār of the village Gurukulavājan. The ninth year of some king is also mentioned in another piece. cells.place: Pūḷiyār temple, south wall.

Nos. 306 and 382 above.

Records a sale of land by the sabhā of Paramēśvaramangalam, a brahmadēya in Vaḍagarai-Poygai-nāḍu in favour of Tiruviraṇīśvaramudāyadēva of Aṭṭuppaḷi-Niyamam in Eyi-nāḍu for 20 kaḻañju received from Malapaḍi-Porpavai, wife of a person (name lost) of Aṭṭuppaḷi-Niyamam, for meeting the expenses of a festival of the god during the Tai-ppūśam festival. The sabhā agreed to pay the annual taxes on the land thus sold. Do.Read more (1 KB)

cells.place: West wall of the same shrine, tier
cells.remarks: Begins with the praśasti, Tirumanni valara, etc., of the king. Records a sale of two mā of land to god Chaṇḍēśvara in Tiruviraṇīśvaram of Aṭṭuppaḷi-Niyamam in Eyi-nāḍu, by the sabhā of Vāḍarāyaṇamangalam, a dēvadāna of Āṇaikkāy-perumāṇār in Pāṇḍyakulāśani-vaḷanāḍu and the dēvadāna of Āṇaikkāy-perumāṇār, for 10 kaḻañju of gold as price for the land, 10 kāśu as ira-kāval and agreed to pay the irai and kudimai on behalf of the temple. This arrangement was necessitated as the latter were not able to pay some taxes in arrears due to failure of the crops.

cells.location: Perumbuliyūr
cells.place: Vyāghrapurīśvara temple. Three fragments built into the walls of the maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Commences with the praśasti, Tirumanni valara, etc., of which the major portion is lost. Records an endowment of 15-1/4 kaḻañju of pon weighed by kaḍaikkāl by Araiyan Kaṇḍan alias Uttama-Chōḷa-mūvēndavēḷār, a dēvakaṇmi of the temple, to the queen Pañchavan-mahādēvi for distributing śattūru to the śivayōgis and tapasyas during the midday worship of god Mahādēva of Perumbuliyūr, a brahmadēya in Poygai-nāḍu in Rājēndraśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu. The Śivabrāhmaṇas who were the paridārakas of the temple invested the money in land and undertook the responsibility of distributing the food.

cells.place:

cells.remarks: Records that the mahāsabhā of Porumbuliyūr, a brahmadeya of Kiļpūļūru in Poygai-nādu, had sold tax-free land, 3 mā in extent, in favour of god Mahādeva of Tirumūniśvaram in the 20th year of the king (Madurai-koṇda Parakēsari (i.e. Parāntaka I), and that having received the sale-price from god Mahādeva of Tiruneyttānam, the same sabhā gave some other land, 6½-mā and kiļ … and māgāṇi in extent in exchange for the former to the god of Tirumūniśvaram. The sabhā further undertook to pay the taxes on this piece of land. Do.

cells.remarks: Right side of the slab is broken. Records a gift of land to god Svayambhū Siddheśvara of Bayinala(?) situated in a division (name lost) consisting of 120 villages by several persons of whom Vaijarasayya, Vitharasayya and Guḍdaġa- madēva are named. cells.place: Slab near the western side of the Āñjanēya temple at the Śriṅgēri-matha.
cells.date: Śaka 1268 (current), Pārthiva, Phālguṇa ba. 1, Thursday = 1346 A.D., March 9.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of nine villages (named given) situated in Kula-nāḍu included in the agrahāra Narasimhapura, 150 gaḍyāṇas towards taxes payable by the cultivators therein, by the king and his brothers, Kampanōdeya, Bukaṇṇōdeya, Mārapodeya, Muddapōdeya, son-in-law Ballappa-daṇḍanāyaka, Kumāra Sōvaṇgodeya and others to Bhāratīrthabharatī and his disciples, and the disciples' disciples. Also states on the occasion of celebrating the victory of the king, that the cultivators of Mēlūhāgi-1000 of Śāntālige-nāḍu were exempted from paying 100 gaḍyāṇas as tax. Liṅgōja, son of Chinna Mallōja, engraved the record. Ibid., Sg. 1.

cells.place: Samo slab
cells.date: Regnal Year 7, Vijaya, Jyeshṭha Amāvāsyā, Monday, solar eclipse, Pushya-nakshatra = Śaka samkramanā 1173 A.D., June 11. The eclipse occurred on Tuesday and the nakshatra onthra ăvṛitti.
cells.remarks: States that mahāpradhāna sēndhihipati hiṟiya-daṇḍanāyaka Mādhayeya-daṇḍanāyakantigaḻu, with the permission, made a gift of (the income derived from) s mellaike of Uppalavāyi, in a village in Gontka-nāṟippaṭ-nādu (1807) which was under his administration, to the temple of Nārāyanēśvara of Chinchavalli for worship and repairs, for offerings and for feeding brāhmaṇas and-khaṇḍika. Further, maḷamada[lē]śvara Kaladēvarasa and mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vīra-Gōmidēvarasa are stated to have made a similar gift of their manneya of Uppalavāvi to the same god (Nārāyanēśvara). Also records that Chaṇḍimarasu, the prabhu of Chinchavalli, and the gauda of the sthāna-vṛitti of Chinchavalli and Uppalavāvi to the sunanda ghaṇṭā-khaṇḍikā and to Tējōnidhi-paṇḍita of Varanasi with the stipulation that the incomes thereby realised be used for worship and repairs in the temple and for feeding the ascetics and teachers in the purāṇa-khaṇḍika and the temple officials.

cells.place:
Bhōgāvati.—Slab erected horizontally
near the temple of Hanumān.
cells.remarks: States that the king's subordinate Jagattungadēva, was governing Eḍedore-2000 as avagavijaya. Seems to record a grant of land by certain gāvuṇḍas. Contains a long prasasti of the king.

cells.place: Slab built into another wall of the Māraṭēśvara temple.
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama 21, Dhātu, Chaitra śu. 1, Sunday=1006 A.D., February 27. The weekday was Wednesday.
cells.remarks: States that when the king was in his military camp on the bank of the river, his preceptor Vikramāditya-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya-Sarvakratuyāji-bhaṭṭa, who had received the daṇḍanāyaka, received from the king the village Kallūru as dakshiṇā on performing the Pañchalaṅgala-kratu, and he, in his turn, made over the village to the brāhmaṇas in the presence of the king. On the same occasion mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Chāvuḍarasa of the Kūṇḍi-viṣaya, who was present, made over himself in the gift of the village Kallūru to the brāhmaṇas and made some other gifts such as 100 mattar of land measured by the rod called the māṇikēśvara-kōlu, house-sites, oilmill etc., to god Svayambhū-Māraṭēśvara of Kallūru. Also a grant of land was made to the same deity by Vāmarasa, the brother-in-law of the royal preceptor.

cells.place: Same slab
cells.date: Year 10, [pra bhava], Māgha ba. 2, Sunday=1148 A.D., February 8.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land made by the mahājanas of agrahāra Rūḍi for the benefit of the temple of Vāsudēva built by Vāsudēvayya, son of Bāciga-daṇḍanāyaka whose genealogy is given. Of the lands granted, one was purchased by them from Caṇḍikabbē, the wife of Candraśēkhara-bhaṭṭa. Also records grants of income from levies on articles such as pepper, ginger, sugar, jaggery etc. to the same deity by the nāḍadēśi and other bodies of agrahāra Rūḍi.

cells.location: Khambada-kōra
cells.place: Slab in a field called Kallu-todane.
cells.date: Śaka 1438, Yuva, 9, dhātu, Mārggaśira śu. 15. Probably =1514 A.D., December 9.
cells.remarks: States that what Vijayappa-voḍeya, son of Ratnappa-voḍeya, was governing Bārākur-rājya, he made a grant of twenty varaha-gadyāṇas equivalent to 50 kāṭi-gadyāṇas towards the amṛtapadi service and burning of a perpetual lamp for the deity Chandranāthasvāmi for the welfare of the King. The amount was to be realised from the siddhāya tax, due to the palace, from a hamlet of Keragālu, a village belonging to the palace treasury.

cells.date: Śaka 1280, Vilambi, Śrāvaṇa śu. 1, Saturday=1358 A.D., July 7, f.d.t. ‘07.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. States that mahāpradhāna Maleya-daṇṇāyaka was ruling over Bārākur-rājya, son of Viranna, made a gift of land called Aneyabalu purchasing it at the then prevailing rates, to god Kiru-man-dīlēśvara for the welfare of the king. cells.location: Tasai
cells.place: Stone built into the well of the Śiva temple. Impressions from the Curator, Government Museum, Alwar.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the temple of god Viṣṇu by Rāṇyāditya, son of Hallavaṇa and Gūlla, grandson of Nāgasvāmin and Gōvā (or Gōchā) and great-grandson of Miya. The eulogy was composed by Dēśaṭa(or Dēgaṭa), son of Bhaṭṭa Dēśaṭa and engraved by the goldsmith Māhaṭa, son of Chāmuṇḍāditya. Also records the grant of 2 mūlas of land and forty ghaṭakas of oil and 200 of saffron for worship. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXVI, pp. 49 ff. and Plates.

cells.location: Kharakhadi
cells.place: Marble stone in the Tughlaq village.
cells.date: Vikrama 1396, Vaiśākha ba. 13, Monday = 1340 A.D., April 24 f.d.t. The month was amānta.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records the construction of a mosque with a well in the village Karkhadi in Vātapadra-dēśa in Lāṭa-dēśa by order of Ulugh Khān, son of Malik Muzaffar, under the local ruler and Mokhāḍa, son of Khēta as the stone mason. For the Persian portion, see A.R. Ep. 1963-64, No 85. Cf. Śrī Pratāpasiṃha Mahārājābhiṣēka Granthamālā, (Muslim Inscriptions), Baroda, pp. 1-2 and p. 16; Bulletin, Mss. and Pict. Gallery, Baroda, Vol. XII (1955-56), pp. 33-35.

cells.place: Mātuji temple
cells.date:
(1) Vikrama 1839, Śāka 1705, Vaiśākha ba. 10, Sunday=1783 A. D., May 25. The month was amānta.
(2) Vikrama 1839, Āśvina śu. 10, Sunday=1783 A. D., October 5.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a new maṇḍapa at a cost of Rs. 6525 for the goddess Barchibāī, as per her ājñā (probably received in the dream) by Mānājirāv Gāyakavāḍ, the brother of the king and its consecration by Rājaguru Nathu-bhaṭṭa of Amadābād and other brāhmaṇas. Also mentions Jōshī Manasārām as the engraver.

cells.place: Akhti-ki-Bāolī

cells.language: Persian verse and prose, Nasta'liq; Sanskrit, Nāgarī.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. States that a garden and a step-well were constructed for public use in the name of Sobhā Chand, son of Sītal Dās Mahājan Agarwal, resident of the gasba (name illegible) during the faujdārī and amāni of Mirzā Ibrāhīm Husain Khān and Rāi Mansukh Karōri respectively. Also mentions, among others, the names of Chandra Bhān and Qamāgis Bān Nūhū, Sukhānand, Kirmā Dās, Champat Rāi and Bhauyya La'l Chand. For the Sanskrit portion, see A.R. Ep., 1962-63, App. B, No. 445.
